cultural_pragmatics.politeness_note: Suara awak merdu 是自然的赞美；对不熟悉的人可说 Suara anda sungguh merdu。朋友之间用 kau 须符合双方平日的相处方式。
cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 适合赞美歌声、乐声、鸟鸣及优美的诵读声。评价宗教诵读时应尊重其宗教性质和场合；反话式地说 merdu 可能被理解为嘲笑。

sociolinguistic_register.politeness_note: Suara awak merdu 是自然的赞美；对不熟悉的人可说 Suara anda sungguh merdu。朋友之间用 kau 须符合双方平日的相处方式。
sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 适合赞美歌声、乐声、鸟鸣及优美的诵读声。评价宗教诵读时应尊重其宗教性质和场合；反话式地说 merdu 可能被理解为嘲笑。

etymology.historical_story: Merdu is traced to Sanskrit mṛdu, meaning soft, gentle, or tender, in [Loan-Words in Indonesian and Malay](https://sealang.net/indonesia/lwim.old/htm/m.htm). Its Malay meaning centres on pleasant sound, especially voices and music. A useful semantic bridge is gentleness experienced through hearing: something agreeable to the ear. This association explains the meaning, but does not identify a particular borrowing date or intermediary language.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 merdu 联想成“美的调”：听到优美的歌声，就想到 suara merdu。

morphology.pattern_note: 未确认其为马来语普通词；作为专名使用时写作 Mirana，不宜拆解为马来语词根和词缀。原始资料未提供音节与读音，故保留空值。

senses.zh_definition: 米拉娜：专有名称，可指《Dota 2》及动画《DOTA：龙之血》中的女性角色；未核实其具有马来语普通词义。
senses.en_definition: A proper name, notably that of a female character in Dota 2 and DOTA: Dragon’s Blood; not verified as a Malay common word.
senses.ms_definition: Nama khas, antaranya nama watak wanita dalam Dota 2 dan DOTA: Dragon’s Blood; makna sebagai kata umum bahasa Melayu belum dapat disahkan. Huraian ini bukan takrif rasmi DBP.
senses.nuances: 正文中须大写为 Mirana。原始资料没有 DBP 释义，检索也未确认普通词条，因此不能标为已获官方确认的马来语词。角色身份可由 [Netflix 官方介绍](https://media.netflix.com/en/only-on-netflix/80994336)确认；但不能据此断定输入词频中的所有实例均指该角色。以下搭配与例句为教学拟写，搭配频率未经语料核实。

etymology.historical_story: Mirana illustrates how fictional names can enter multilingual texts without becoming ordinary vocabulary. Netflix identifies Princess Mirana in its official synopsis for DOTA: Dragon’s Blood. That establishes a character reference, but does not establish a Malay lexical meaning or the name’s linguistic origin. No historical derivation is asserted here. Source: [Netflix Media Center](https://media.netflix.com/en/only-on-netflix/80994336).

morphology.pattern_note: 词干末尾的 k 与后缀开头的 k 都保留，所以写 kk；马来西亚常见发音中，前一个 k 可实现为喉塞音。与名词 masakan 的单 k 区别。headword.jawi 依输入保留为 ماسق，但这是 masak 的拼写；加上 -kan 后，派生词应写作 ماسقکن。

senses.zh_definition: 为某人烹煮或准备食物。
senses.en_definition: To cook or prepare food for someone.
senses.ms_definition: Memasak atau menyediakan makanan untuk seseorang.
senses.nuances: 这里的 -kan 表示受益关系。常见于请求、命令及第一、第二人称被动结构，如 Tolong masakkan saya bubur 和 Bubur itu saya masakkan untuk ibu。普通主动陈述通常使用 memasakkan。拼写依据 [DBP：masak + -kan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=masak+kan)。

collocations.en: cook rice for a younger sibling

senses.zh_definition: 把食物煮熟，或继续烹煮至熟透。
senses.en_definition: To make food cooked or cook it through.
senses.ms_definition: Menjadikan makanan masak atau membuat supaya makanan masak sepenuhnya.
senses.nuances: 这里的 -kan 表示使成义，重点是达到熟透的状态。不要把 masak 的“水果成熟”“经验老到”等所有词义直接搬到本词。较旧文体中，memasakkan 还可比喻仔细考虑或使事情成熟。依据 [DBP：memasakkan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=memasakkan)。

etymology.historical_story: The dictionary places ripeness and cooked food together under masak, linking fruit ready to eat with food made ready by heat. Adding -kan gives masakkan its practical household meanings: cook for someone or make something cooked. The spelling preserves both adjoining k letters, distinguishing an act of cooking from masakan, the food or cuisine produced.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: masak“熟”＋-kan“使熟／替人做”：两个 k，一边连着锅里的食物，一边连着等饭的人。

morphology.formula: meN- + stabilkan → menstabilkan; 完整分析：meN- + stabil + -kan → menstabilkan
morphology.pattern_note: 按输入保留 stabilkan 为直接构词基础；更底层词根是 stabil。meN- 在借词起首辅音群 /st/ 前实现为 men-，保留 s；-kan 表示使成为某种状态。

word_family.gloss: 稳定剂；稳定器；稳定因素

senses.zh_definition: 使稳定、平稳或稳固；使价格、状况、运动或其他变化减少波动。
senses.en_definition: To make something stable, steady or settled; to reduce its fluctuations.
senses.ms_definition: Menjadikan stabil, iaitu tidak berubah-ubah, tenang atau mantap; memantapkan.
senses.nuances: 及物动词，常接 harga、ekonomi、keadaan 或 kedudukan 等宾语。表示主动使某物稳定；描述某物自身变得稳定通常用 menjadi stabil。释义及词族依据 [PRPM：stabil](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=351284&keyword=stabil)。

sociolinguistic_register.politeness_note: 属于中性、较正式的技术及行政用语，适合报告、解释措施和说明设备功能。日常交谈也可按语境说 bagi stabil 或 pegang bagi tak bergerak。
sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 用于价格、经济、设备位置及其他需要减少波动的对象。谈到人的情绪时，menenangkan 往往更贴切；直接说某人“不稳定”可能带有负面评价。

etymology.historical_story: DBP identifies stabil as an English-derived Malay adjective. Malay then builds menstabilkan with its own verbal morphology, alongside kestabilan, penstabilan and penstabil. This family illustrates how a borrowed base becomes productive in Malay: the adjective describes a stable condition, while the derived verb expresses causing that condition. [PRPM：stabil](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=351284&keyword=stabil)。
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: stabil＝稳定；-kan 加上“使”的意思；meN- 构成主动动词：menstabilkan＝使它稳定下来。记住 st 一起保留。

morphology.pattern_note: 词首 p 在 meN- 派生中脱落，鼻音实现为 m。root_word 与 root_jawi 按要求保留输入值；实际构词词根为 puncak（ڤونچق），输入的 is_root: true 有误。

sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 用于情绪或局势时语气较强，应有足够上下文支持。朋友间可夸张使用，但描述上司、长辈或敏感冲突时宜保持客观。

etymology.historical_story: Memuncak is formed from puncak, meaning a summit or highest point. Malay extends this vertical image to less visible experiences: anger rises, tension mounts, and prices climb. The prefix meN- turns the summit image into a process, with the initial p replaced by m. This explains the modern formation without requiring a speculative ancient origin. [DBP: puncak](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=399108&keyword=puncak)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 抓住 puncak“顶峰”：meN- 让它动起来，p 换成 m，memuncak 就是一路冲向高峰。

morphology.pattern_note: 直接基底为输入中的 melaporkan，最终词根为 lapor；meN- 遇 l 实现为 me-，l 保留。-nya 是宾语附着代词，此处 suffix 是字段归类。输入 jawi 仅对应 melaporkan；完整词形应补写为 ملاڤورکنڽ。

senses.zh_definition: 报告、汇报或报道它／那件事；依上下文也可指举报该人。

etymology.historical_story: Melaporkannya illustrates how Malay builds a complete expression around a reporting verb. The base lapor forms melaporkan, and the attached pronoun -nya points back to something or someone already mentioned. What English often expresses as two words, 'report it', appears here as one written word. Its meaning therefore depends on the surrounding discourse rather than a separate historical anecdote. [DBP: melaporkan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=melaporkan)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 先记 melaporkan“报告”，再把 nya 想成回指箭头：把刚才那件事报告上去。

senses.zh_definition: 哺乳动物：属于哺乳纲的脊椎动物，具有毛发和四腔心脏，雌性以乳腺分泌的乳汁哺育幼体。
senses.en_definition: A vertebrate of the class Mammalia, characterized by hair, a four-chambered heart and milk-producing mammary glands in females.
senses.ms_definition: Haiwan bertulang belakang, badannya berbulu, jantungnya terbahagi kepada empat kebuk, dan menyusui anaknya.
senses.nuances: 可指一只哺乳动物，也可统称该类动物；数量由上下文表达。不能把胎生当作无例外的定义条件：鸭嘴兽和针鼹会产卵。鲸类也是哺乳动物，人类同样属于此类。马来语释义据 Kamus Dewan Edisi Keempat 展开缩写。依据：[PRPM：mamalia](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=243192&keyword=mamalia)。

etymology.historical_story: The international scientific name Mammalia was introduced by Linnaeus in 1758 and derives from Latin mamma, meaning breast or teat. Its memorable organizing feature is milk production, which connects animals as different as bats, whales and humans. Malay mamalia shares this scientific vocabulary; the evidence cited here does not establish its immediate borrowing language. [Schiebinger's historical study](https://shipseducation.net/tnos/library/Schiebinger1993-mammals.pdf).

etymology.historical_story: Minion entered English from Middle French mignon, meaning a darling or favourite. Early uses concerned someone enjoying a powerful person's favour. The word later acquired the less flattering image of an obedient, insignificant subordinate. This history helps explain why calling a colleague a minion can sting even when the speaker intends a joke. [Merriam-Webster word history](https://art19.com/shows/merriam-websters-word-of-the-day/episodes/ed1e9c79-1b34-4ab7-85e8-80088d1b438c)

etymology.historical_story: Mimpinya illustrates how Malay attaches a short pronoun to an ordinary noun. The base mimpi covers both sleeping experiences and figurative imaginings; adding -nya identifies whose dream is meant without specifying gender. The form therefore joins two familiar storytelling needs: describing an unseen experience and linking it to a person already introduced in the conversation.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: mimpi 是“梦”，尾巴 -nya 是“他／她的”：mimpi + nya，把梦挂到那个人名下。

etymology.historical_story: The dictionary family centres on rempuh, with merempuh naming the action and rempuhan its impact or onrush. Its meanings connect bodily movement through resistance with violent collision. The expression merempuh maut extends that physical image to someone pressing forward despite mortal danger. This explains the semantic connection without proposing an undocumented ancient origin.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 读到 rem-puh，想象身体冲过障碍后发出“砰”的一声：强闯，也能撞上。声音联想仅作助记。

etymology.historical_story: Membutakan is a transparent Malay formation built from buta, meaning blind, with the active prefix meN- and causative suffix -kan. Its imagery also supports figurative expressions: just as damaged sight prevents physical seeing, greed or anger can prevent sound judgment. This connection makes the physical and moral senses easy to understand together.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 抓住 buta＝看不见：mem-...-kan 把状态变成使成动作，membutakan 就是“使看不见”，也可指“蒙蔽判断”。

etymology.historical_story: Maaf belongs to the Arabic-derived vocabulary of pardon used in Malay. The longer form shows how borrowed vocabulary participates in Malay grammar: maaf combines with -kan, then the particle -lah. Its cultural resonance is especially clear in requests for forgiveness, including festive greetings, where familiar words carry both personal feeling and social responsibility.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 分三步记：maaf＝宽恕，maafkan＝原谅，maafkanlah＝“请原谅吧”。末尾 lah 像把请求轻轻递给对方。

etymology.historical_story: The image behind membebankan is the beban, a load that must be carried. Malay uses this concrete image for duties, expenses, and emotional strain as well as physical weight. The construction makes the relationship visible: something becomes a burden borne by someone. This explains why both assigning responsibility and causing hardship belong within its meaning.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 beban 想成肩上的重担：meN- + beban + -kan，就是“把重担加上去”，所以能说加任务、加费用、加压力。

etymology.historical_story: Madeline is an English form of French Madeleine, itself a form of Magdalene. Its name history ultimately connects with the place name Magdala. Another cultural association comes from Ludwig Bemelmans's children's books: their heroine is Madeline, and the series began in 1939. These are naming and literary connections rather than Malay word formation. [Madeline](https://www.behindthename.com/name/madeline), [Madeleine](https://www.behindthename.com/name/madeleine)

etymology.historical_story: Laung names a loud call used to summon people or attract attention. Malay morphology turns that call into melaungkan, directing attention to what is shouted. The dictionary also records public advocacy, linking a voice carrying across a gathering with an idea reaching a wider audience. No securely established borrowing history is supplied here; the transparent Malay derivation explains the word.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: laung＝响亮呼声；me- + laung + -kan＝把内容喊出来。记住 melaung 是“喊”，melaungkan slogan 是“喊口号”。

etymology.historical_story: Malay dictionaries place melencong under lencong and record both physical deviation and departure from an intended purpose. The connection offers a familiar conceptual bridge: a discussion can leave its course just as a traveller can leave a route. This explains the related senses without establishing which developed first. See [DBP's word-family entry](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=lencong).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 读到 /mə.len.tʃoŋ/，想象一条线突然拐弯：车走偏是 melencong，话题拐走也是 melencong。

morphology.pattern_note: root_word 按输入保留直接基词 mengecewakan，其词汇词根为 kecewa。meN- 接 kecewa 时，词首 k 脱落，形成 mengecewakan。-mu 是表示第二人称宾语的附着代词；此处 suffix 仅表示其后附位置。输入 Jawi 未含 -mu，完整词形补为 مڠچيواکنمو。[DBP 构词示例](https://eseminar.dbp.gov.my/dokumen/koleksi1.pdf)

senses.zh_definition: 使你失望；因未能满足你的期待而令你感到失落或难过。

senses.ms_definition: Menyebabkan kamu berasa kecewa, hampa atau dukacita kerana harapan kamu tidak dipenuhi.
senses.nuances: -mu 在此表示承受动作的“你”，不是“你的”。该词表示“使你失望”，不是“对你感到失望”；后者可说 kecewa dengan kamu。基词中“使计划落空”的义项不应机械地全部移植到这个以人为宾语的词形。

etymology.historical_story: Mengecewakanmu brings together two productive Malay resources: a causative verb and an attached personal pronoun. DBP illustrates the formation of mengecewakan from kecewa through the regular change affecting initial k. Adding -mu makes the disappointment personally directed at the listener. This compact form fits heartfelt promises and apologies, while its complete pronunciation can give a message a literary tone. [Source](https://eseminar.dbp.gov.my/dokumen/koleksi1.pdf)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: kecewa＝失望；mengecewakan＝使人失望；句尾 mu＝你。连起来就是“让你失望”。

senses.zh_definition: 凭既有印象认出我；辨认出我的身份。
senses.en_definition: To recognize me from previous knowledge or acquaintance.
senses.ms_definition: Mengecam diri aku berdasarkan rupa, suara, atau pengetahuan yang sedia ada.
senses.nuances: 着重“认得出”，不一定表示关系熟悉。-ku 是动作的宾语，因此 dia mengenalku 是“他认得我”。词义参照 [DBP：mengenal](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=mengenal)，并结合输入中的 Kamus Dewan 释义转述。

senses.zh_definition: 认识我；对我的身份、为人或经历有所了解。

senses.ms_definition: Mengetahui siapa aku atau mempunyai hubungan perkenalan dengan aku.
senses.nuances: 与“认出我”不同，此义可以指持续的相识关系。mengenalku 不自动表示深知内心；表达深入了解时，可加 dengan baik。

etymology.historical_story: Mengenalku brings together the verb mengenal and the compact pronoun -ku, referring to aku. This attachment lets a speaker place the self directly inside an expression of recognition or acquaintance. In Malaysian usage, its compactness suits personal narration and expressive writing, while everyday conversation often uses the separate words kenal aku. See [DBP on attached pronouns](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=kau+pasif).

morphology.formula: miliki + -nya → milikinya；更深层：milik + -i → miliki；主动陈述式：meN- + milik + -i + -nya → memilikinya
morphology.pattern_note: 保留输入词基 miliki；更深层词根为 milik。-i 添加后 k 位于元音之间，读 /k/。-nya 是后附代词，此处通常指宾语“它”，并非派生词缀；suffix 标示其后附位置。输入未提供 Jawi，保留 null。

senses.zh_definition: 拥有它；取得它的所有权，通常用于劝告、邀请或促销性质的祈使语。
senses.en_definition: Own it or acquire it, typically as an invitation or imperative.
senses.ms_definition: Jadikan sesuatu itu hak milik sendiri atau punyainya, lazimnya sebagai suruhan atau pelawaan.
senses.nuances: 词义按 [DBP：milik](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=54140&keyword=milik) 中 memiliki 的释义及 miliki + -nya 的结构综合转述，并非声称 DBP 单列此词形。普通主动陈述句应使用 memilikinya；口语或创作中可见省略 meN- 的 milikinya。它不同于 miliknya，后者通常表示“他／她的所有物”。

etymology.historical_story: Milikinya is a transparent Malay formation rather than a separate root: milik supplies ownership, -i forms the verb, and -nya points back to its object. Its cultural setting is especially visible in advertising, where ownership becomes an invitation. A Malaysian housing advertorial used milikinya sekarang to present a homeownership offer. See [the housing advertorial](https://www.malaysiakini.com/advertorial/546166).

etymology.historical_story: DBP distinguishes two bases spelled iring: one concerns following, the other a side or flank. Both produce mengiring through the regular Malay nasal prefix. This explains why the same written word can describe someone lying sideways or an attendant escorting a guest. Sentence structure and context identify the intended meaning; spelling alone cannot separate these dictionary senses.

etymology.historical_story: Mengeja combines the Malay verbal prefix meN- with eja. An older account of Malay orthography connects eja with the Arabic spelling term hijā and describes spelling as dividing a word into its components. That historical classroom image survives in today's familiar task of naming a word's letters one by one. [Source: historical Malay orthography text](https://www.sabrizain.org/malaya/library/malayorthography.pdf).

etymology.historical_story: The history belongs to kahwin, not to the attached pronoun. In his 1852 Malay dictionary, John Crawfurd recorded kawin and identified it as Persian in origin. Modern Malaysian spelling uses kahwin, while Malay morphology produces mengahwini and then mengahwininya. The form thus combines an established marriage word with productive Malay grammar; it is not a separate borrowing with its own independent origin.

etymology.historical_story: French madame combines ma, meaning my, with dame, meaning lady. The Académie française dates the word to the twelfth century and records its development as a courtesy title. Its history explains the literal connection with my lady, but modern speakers use it as an established form of address. The French plural is mesdames. [Source: Académie française](https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A9M0093).

etymology.historical_story: Mengenalimu illustrates how Malay builds a personal expression from ordinary grammatical parts. Kenal supplies recognition or acquaintance, mengenali develops the verbal meaning, and the attached pronoun mu directs it toward the listener. This compact construction helps explain its intimate literary tone: a complete relationship between knowing and being addressed is carried within one written word.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: kenal 是“认识”，mengenali 是“认识、了解”，再接 -mu“你”：mengenalimu＝认识你。

etymology.historical_story: Menggerudi is transparently formed from gerudi with the Malay active prefix meN-. Its two supplied dictionary senses connect workshop drilling with the much larger task of boring into the earth or seabed for oil. The shared idea is making a hole with drilling equipment; the supplied evidence does not establish the deeper origin of gerudi.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 记住 gerudi 是“钻具”，前面加表示主动动作的 meng-，就是“动手钻孔”；g 保留，拼成 meng-gerudi。

etymology.historical_story: Menelannya is a grammatical formation rather than a separate ancient root. Its base menelan comes from telan through nasal prefixation; the attached pronoun -nya supplies the object. Dictionary meanings extend bodily swallowing to expenditure, reluctant acceptance, conquest, and disappearance, linking several abstract experiences to one concrete action. [PRPM: telan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=telan)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: telan＝吞；meN- 加上去，t 被鼻音替换；-nya＝它：menelannya 就是“把它吞下”，也可比喻“忍下这件事”。

morphology.pattern_note: meN- 在 c 前写作 men-，词根开头的 c 保留；c 表示 /tʃ/。

etymology.historical_story: Mencakar is transparently formed from cakar, the Malay word for a claw, with the active verbal prefix meN-. Its dictionary senses connect the same physical movement with both scratching and a chicken's search for food. The related expression pencakar langit extends the clawing image upward to describe a skyscraper.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 先记 cakar＝爪；加上 meN-，就把静态的“爪”变成动态的“用爪抓”。

morphology.pattern_note: 按输入保留直接基底 menari；更深层词根是 tari，接 meN- 时首音 t 脱落，形成 menari。-lah 是附着在词后的强调小品词，并非派生词缀；affix_type 的 suffix 仅表示其后附位置。音节为 me.na.ri.lah，输入未提供，故 syllables 保留 null。输入 jawi 未含 -lah；完整形式为 مناريله。参见 [DBP：lah](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?d=175768&keyword=lah)。

senses.zh_definition: 跳舞吧；请跳舞。以 menari 加强调小品词 -lah，表达邀请、劝促、许可或命令。
senses.en_definition: Dance; do dance, with -lah adding invitation, encouragement, permission, or insistence.
senses.ms_definition: Melakukan gerak tari mengikut irama muzik, dengan partikel -lah yang menegaskan ajakan, suruhan atau galakan mengikut konteks.
senses.nuances: 核心动作是 menari；-lah 的效果取决于语境和语调，并不必然表示客气。该词整体仍为动词，不能因含 -lah 就归类为 particle。输入引文虽有 ark 标记，DBP《Kamus Pelajar》也收录普通跳舞义，不能据此把现代 menari 一概视为古语。参见 [DBP：menari](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=menari) 与 [DBP：-lah 的语法说明](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?d=175768&keyword=lah)。

messages.speaker: Farah (朋友)
messages.ms_spoken: Menarilah sekali, Amir. Tak payah malu, kita cuba je!
messages.ms_standard: Menarilah bersama kami, Amir. Tidak perlu malu; kita cuba sahaja.
messages.zh: Amir，一起来跳嘛。不用害羞，试试就好！
messages.en: Come dance with us, Amir. Don't be shy. Let's just give it a go!

messages.speaker: Amir (朋友)
messages.ms_spoken: Boleh, tapi aku nak tengok langkah dulu, ya.
messages.ms_standard: Baiklah, tetapi saya hendak melihat langkah tarian terlebih dahulu.
messages.zh: 可以，不过我想先看看舞步啊。
messages.en: Sure, but let me watch the steps first.

cultural_pragmatics.politeness_note: -lah 不保证礼貌。面对不熟悉的人，可说 Jika sudi, menarilah bersama kami，表达“如果愿意，请和我们一起跳”；不要把反复劝说当作热情的必要表现。
cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 适用于舞蹈教学、表演邀请和朋友互动。邀舞应尊重对方的意愿、身体接触界限及个人或宗教习惯；对方拒绝后应接受。

etymology.historical_story: Menarilah combines the dance verb menari with the attached particle -lah. Beneath menari lies tari: Malay nasal prefixation removes the initial t when forming the verb. Adding -lah then changes the utterance's force rather than naming a new dance. In an invitation, the result can sound encouraging; in an instruction, it can make the direction more emphatic.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 分两步记：tari 是“舞”，menari 是“跳舞”；末尾接 lah，想成招手说“来跳吧”。

morphology.pattern_note: 作为借入的完整词根记忆，不拆为马来语词缀；sy 表示一个辅音 /ʃ/。下列词族成员为复合称谓，不是加词缀形成的派生词。

word_family.gloss: 赛事秩序与安全工作人员

senses.zh_definition: 元帅；某些国家军制中的最高级军事长官或最高级军衔。
senses.en_definition: A marshal: a military officer holding the highest rank in certain armed forces.
senses.ms_definition: Pegawai tertinggi dalam tentera; jeneral besar.
senses.nuances: 指特定军制中的军衔或高级军事身份，不宜泛指所有将军或军事指挥官。marsyal tentera darat 对应陆军元帅。释义依据 [DBP：marsyal](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=marsyal)。

senses.zh_definition: 活动秩序或安全工作人员，尤指负责监督比赛进程、引导参赛者及维持赛道秩序的赛事工作人员。
senses.en_definition: An official who supervises an event and maintains order or safety, especially at a race.
senses.ms_definition: Pegawai yang mengawal atau menyelia perjalanan sesuatu acara umum, terutama acara sukan seperti perlumbaan kereta.
senses.nuances: 常见于赛车、路跑、骑行及其他大型活动。职责可包括指示路线、展示旗号或协助安全管理；不能一概译成负责判定成绩的“裁判”。此义同见 [DBP：marsyal](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=marsyal)。

collocations.zh: 遵从赛事工作人员的指示

dual_scenarios.context: 赛事通告 / 新闻报道
dual_scenarios.ms: Penganjur menempatkan marsyal di setiap selekoh berbahaya untuk memantau keadaan litar dan memberi isyarat kepada pelumba.
dual_scenarios.zh: 主办方在每个危险弯道安排赛事工作人员，监控赛道情况并向车手发出信号。
dual_scenarios.en: The organisers stationed marshals at every dangerous bend to monitor track conditions and signal to the drivers.

dual_scenarios.context: WhatsApp / 朋友参加路跑
dual_scenarios.ms_spoken: Ikut arahan marsyal kat depan tu, jangan main lintas je.
dual_scenarios.ms_standard: Ikutlah arahan marsyal di hadapan itu dan jangan melintas sesuka hati.
dual_scenarios.zh: 听前面工作人员的指示啦，别随便穿过去。
dual_scenarios.en: Follow the marshal's instructions up ahead. Don't just cross whenever you feel like it.
spoken_features: kat depan 对应 di hadapan
tu 对应 itu
jangan main…je 表示提醒对方不要贸然行事

messages.speaker: Hakim (朋友)
messages.ms_spoken: Aku dah sampai simpang. Nak ikut mana ni?
messages.ms_standard: Saya sudah sampai di simpang. Arah manakah yang perlu saya ikut?
messages.zh: 我到岔路口了。现在该往哪边走啊？
messages.en: I'm at the junction. Which way do I go?

messages.speaker: Mei (朋友)
messages.ms_spoken: Tanya marsyal kat situ je. Dia pakai vest oren.
messages.ms_standard: Tanya sahaja marsyal di situ. Dia memakai ves berwarna jingga.
messages.zh: 问那边的工作人员就行。他穿着橙色背心。
messages.en: Just ask the marshal there—the one in the orange vest.

cultural_pragmatics.politeness_note: 称呼赛事工作人员可说 encik、puan 或直接礼貌询问。涉及军人时，应使用对方实际的军衔与称谓，不能把 marsyal 当成所有军官的通用称呼。
cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 先根据军队、赛道或公共活动等语境判断词义。赛事中的 marsyal 是具体工作岗位，应配合其现场指引；不要仅凭这一称谓推断其具有警察身份。

etymology.historical_story: Marsyal corresponds to English marshal, whose history runs through French to Germanic words meaning horse and servant. A role associated with horses developed into high court and military office. Malay records both the senior military sense and the event-supervision sense, linking command with organised movement. See [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/marshal) and [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=marsyal).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 marsyal 联想到英语 marshal：军队里统筹指挥，赛场上统筹秩序；共同画面是“有人负责让全场有序”。
